subject: Rebaseline: AcmeCorp POC scope and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery — POC next steps / success criteria

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps for the POC so we have a single source of truth. Attaching an initial success-criteria workbook.

Summary of agreed items:
- POC duration: 4 weeks (kickoff target 2026-09-07)
- Primary use case: customer support triage (classify intent + provide suggested responses)
- Success criteria (initial):
  * Intent classification accuracy >= 88% on your labeled set (test split)
  * Average generation latency <= 450ms p50 for 512-token requests
  * End-to-end throughput to support 20 QPS in steady state
- Evaluation plan: weekly evals using the shared eval set, daily logs to be uploaded to the shared Drive folder, and a mid-POC quality review at end of week 2
- Ownership:
  * Redwood: model hosting, instrumentation, conservative caching config; contact: Rishi
  * AcmeCorp: test data preparation, network firewall / VPC peering, and labeling clarifications; contact: Sam / Priya
- Next steps:
  1) Sam to share test dataset and any network constraints (by 2026-08-28)
  2) Redwood to provide initial deployment plan and a tentative timeline for kickoff (by 2026-08-30)
  3) Schedule kickoff call for week of 2026-09-07

Attachments: acmecorp_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (initial draft)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery — POC next steps / success criteria

Marissa — thanks for the recap. This lines up with what we discussed; a couple of asks from our side after syncing with the engineering team: 

1) Add a secondary use case mid-POC: routing to the correct internal team based on intent (this will be lower throughput but critical for validation). Would like it added to success criteria as a stretch goal.
2) Latency target: our ops team asked if we can tighten p50 to <= 350ms for 256-token requests (these are our most common queries). If that tightens the hardware needs, flag it and we can discuss budget.
3) Network: we can start the VPC peering work but need a network diagram from your infra team and a list of IPs/ports required.

We'll aim to share the labeled test set by 2026-08-28 but the routing use case will need a small additional labeled sample (~1k rows) that our CS team will prioritize next week.

Thanks — Sam

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery — POC next steps / success criteria

Thanks Sam — good notes. Quick thoughts on the rebaseline and feasibility: 

- Adding routing as a secondary use case: fine — we'll treat it as a tier-2 success criterion (stretch) with a smaller labeled set; we’ll validate on the 1k sample you mentioned.
- Latency: p50 <= 350ms for 256 tokens is aggressive but doable with the right instance type + quantized model. Expect a small increase in cost (~15-25%) relative to the baseline config. We can run an optimization pass during week 1 to tune batching and KV cache for those shorter requests.
- Network docs: attaching our standard network requirements doc (acme_network_requirements.pdf). Please confirm whether you require a peered VPC or NAT egress; both have different setup timelines.

Proposed rebaseline (high level):
- POC duration: unchanged (4 weeks)
- Deliverables: weekly eval reports + a final report that includes performance vs. success criteria; Week 2 mid-point review to decide whether to expand routing test size
- New success criteria (updated):
  * Intent classification accuracy >= 88% (unchanged)
  * Generation latency p50 <= 350ms for 256-token requests (updated target)
  * Throughput requirement remains 20 QPS for peak, but routing throughput can be validated at 5 QPS

Action items:
- Acme: confirm whether you’ll do VPC peering or NAT (Sam / Priya)
- Acme: share the 1k labeled routing sample and main eval set by 2026-08-28
- Redwood: provide a revised success-criteria workbook and updated kickoff timeline by 2026-08-30 (I’ll own delivery)

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Rebaseline confirmed — updated POC plan and next steps

Sam / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Rishi's note, we’ve re-baselined the POC to include the routing use case as a stretch goal and tightened the latency target. I’ve attached an updated success criteria workbook (acmecorp_poc_success_criteria.xlsx) with the changes tracked. High-level updates below: 

- Kickoff: target week of 2026-09-07 (we’ll send a calendar invite once Peering/NAT choice is confirmed)
- Updated success criteria:
  * Intent accuracy >= 88% (test split)
  * Gen latency p50 <= 350ms for 256-token requests
  * Throughput: 20 QPS primary; routing validation at 5 QPS
- Ownership:
  * Redwood (Rishi): infra, model ops, weekly evals, mid-point report
  * Redwood (Marissa): project coordination, weekly business check-ins
  * Acme (Sam/Priya): dataset delivery, VPC peering/NAT config, labeling for routing sample
- Timeline adjustments: if Acme chooses VPC peering, we can still hit kickoff 2026-09-07; if NAT egress is required we may need a one-week delay for firewall rules (tentative new kickoff 2026-09-14).

Next steps (owner / due dates):
1) Acme: confirm peering approach and share routing sample + main eval set (Sam/Priya) — due 2026-08-28 (pending)
2) Redwood: final success criteria workbook (attached) + kickoff invite — due 2026-08-30 (attached)
3) Tech sync: Rishi + Acme infra to schedule network configuration call (to happen before kickoff)

Attachments: acmecorp_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (updated), acme_network_requirements.pdf

If this matches your expectations I’ll lock the dates and send invites.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
